title: Capacity Umbrella: Transient Hedging, Tenant Throttling, and Graceful Reclamation
creator: Marcus Nguyen
summary: Introduce a 'Capacity Umbrella' control plane overlay for Dedicated capacity that provides transient hedging credits, tenant throttling policies, and a graceful reclamation (eviction/quota) mechanism. The feature reduces noisy-neighbor impact and enables controlled bursts without sacrificing SLOs for reserved tenants.
problem_statement: Reserved pools today provide capacity guarantees but lack an elastic overlay for short-lived bursts and coordinated reclamation. Tenants that experience sudden spikes either overload shared capacity or suffer immediate hard throttling, leading to latency SLO violations and support incidents. We need a predictable, auditable mechanism to allow bounded bursts while preserving isolation guarantees.
goals: Allow tenants to absorb short bursty traffic (> baseline) using a proportional transient credit pool (hedging) up to a configured window
Provide tenant-level throttling policies that gracefully escalate from soft-shedding to hard-eviction to protect reserved SLOs
Expose API and Console controls to configure umbrella parameters (credit budget, window length, refill rate, reclaim priority) per-reservation
Ensure observability: per-tenant credit usage, reclamation events, cost delta, and SLO impact metrics
Offer a rollout path with canary/beta tenants and automatic rollback if platform SLOs degrade
non_goals: Replace long-term autoscale contracts or change committed reservation sizing semantics
Provide unlimited bursting or bypass billing/quotas—this is bounded by configured credits
Deliver complex cross-tenant economic settlement for borrowed credits in this initial phase
success_metrics: Reduce P50/P95 latency SLO violations caused by neighbor bursts by 60% in pilot tenants
Cut urgent support tickets for transient capacity contention by 50% within 8 weeks of rollout
Average reserved-pool eviction events per week decrease by 70% for launched pools
At least 3 paying customers adopt umbrella controls in beta with configured credit budgets
user_stories: As a tenant admin I can configure a transient credit budget and window so my service can absorb short spikes without manual intervention
As a Redwood operator I can see a ranked list of ongoing reclamation events and pause umbrella borrowing globally in emergencies
As an SRE I can define throttling escalation rules (soft-shed -> rate-limit -> preemptive reclaim) attached to a reservation
As a Product Manager I can measure the cost delta for burst credits and export per-customer billing adjustments
functional_requirements: FR-1: Add 'umbrella' object to reservation config with fields: credit_budget_tokens, window_seconds, refill_rate, reclaim_priority, allow_burst boolean
FR-2: Centralized credit ledger service that tracks per-reservation credit balances and provides atomic debit/credit operations
FR-3: Runtime hook that checks umbrella credits at request admission and consumes credits proportionally to token cost and latency class
FR-4: Throttling escalation engine with configurable thresholds (soft_shed_pct, rate_limit_pct, reclaim_threshold) and per-tenant policies
FR-5: Reclamation API that triggers graceful model instance drain, snapshot KV-caches if supported, and evicts lowest-priority ephemeral work units
FR-6: Console: edit reservation umbrella settings, view credit history, open reclamation timeline, set auto-replenish options
FR-7: Billing export: annotate usage records with umbrella_credit_consumed and cost_center tags
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-1: Credit ledger operations < 50ms p95 for reads and < 150ms p95 for writes under normal load
NFR-2: Runtime admission check should add < 1ms median overhead per request
NFR-3: All umbrella events must be logged and retained per compliance retention policy (configurable)
NFR-4: System must degrade to conservative hard-throttling policy if ledger becomes unavailable
NFR-5: Role-based access controls for editing umbrella settings (only entitlement admins and SREs)
api_endpoints: GET /reservations/{id}/umbrella - fetch current umbrella state (balance, last_refill, usage_history)
GET /system/umbrella/events - stream recent reclamation and borrow events (paginated)
console_changes: New 'Umbrella' tab on Reservation detail page with: slider for credit_budget_tokens, TTL/window selector, percent-scaling refill rate, reclaim priority picker
Timeline UI showing borrow/replenish/reclaim events with links to logs and associated traces
Alerting toggles for when credit usage > 75%/90%/100% within the window
autoscale_behavior: Autoscaling remains responsible for baseline capacity. Umbrella borrowing does not trigger instant autoscale events in initial release; it is an overlay that consumes transient headroom. A future iteration may allow umbrella thresholds to inform autoscaling decisions via a separate signal.
eviction_policy: Graceful reclamation proceeds in stages: 1) mark low-priority ephemeral work units as 'soft-evict' allowing 10s drain, 2) incrementally throttle new requests for the tenant, 3) if reclaim threshold persists, preempt ephemeral slots and perform hard-evict on oldest ephemeral activations. Eviction respects reclaim_priority; reserved tenant critical tasks exempt when marked critical.
predictive_warmup: We will seed predictive warmup signals into the umbrella controller: when inbound traffic rises with a characteristic pattern (X tokens/min over 3 samples), the system may pre-authorize a small additional credit allotment up to a safety cap to reduce cold-starts. Predictive warmup is opt-in per-reservation in beta.
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-reservation metrics: umbrella_credit_balance, credit_consumed_per_minute, borrow_events_count, reclaim_events_count
Platform metrics aggregated: total_borrowed_tokens, percent_reservations_using_umbrella, average_reclaim_latency
Traces: link reclamation operations to request traces to measure SLO before/after reclaim
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Admin can enable umbrella on a reservation and set credit_budget_tokens, window_seconds, and refill_rate through API and Console
AC-2: Under a synthetic burst (2x baseline for 30s) a reservation with umbrella configured consumes credits instead of failing requests up to credit budget
AC-3: When credits deplete, throttling escalation behaves according to policy (soft-shed -> rate-limit -> reclaim) and is observable via events
AC-4: Credit ledger durability validated by fault-injection tests: on transient controller failure, system falls back to hard-throttle and logs incident
AC-5: Metrics emitted for every borrow/reclaim event and surfaced in Console within 60s
AC-6: No measurable increase (>1ms p50) in request latency introduced by umbrella admission checks in production canary
AC-7: RBAC prevents non-entitled users from editing umbrella configurations
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal alpha): implement ledger + runtime hook + console stub; run smoke tests in staging
Phase 1 (Canary): enable umbrella for 2 internal reserved pools with low customer exposure for 2 weeks; validate stability and metrics
Phase 2 (Beta): invite 3 customer tenants (billing + SRE agreement) for opt-in beta; monitor SLOs and support feedback
Phase 3 (General): Gradual enablement by reservation with default umbrella off; launch docs, pricing note, and runbook
Rollback triggers: platform SLO degradation > 5% increase in P95 latency, >3 incidents from reclamation, or ledger error rate >1%
risks: Incorrect credit accounting could cause tenants to bypass reservation guarantees (mitigate with strong tests and audits)
Rapid global enabling could increase costs—mitigate via opt-in beta and rate-limits
Ledger performance issues could add latency—mitigate by caching read-only balances in the runtime and providing conservative fallback
open_questions: What is the canonical billing model for transient credits—post-paid metered consumption, or pre-purchased credit bundles?
Should umbrella borrowing ever be allowed across reservations owned by the same customer (cross-reservation pooling)?
What default reclaim_priority should we set for ephemeral vs production-critical work?
